newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Islamists vow to stay in power.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Islamists vow to stay in power.

text.p: Turkey's ruling Islamists on Thursday vowed to stay in government despite mounting military-led pressure to step down in a row with the army over religious activism.
"I believe the government has work to do and it will keep on doing it," Ahmet Tekdal, an assistant head of the Islam-based Welfare Party, told a news conference.
Istanbul shares fell 6.85 percent to 1,427 at the close of morning trade on worries that Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition was crumbling.
Two ministers from the secularist wing of the alliance are in open rebellion against Islamist Erbakan for his failure to implement an anti-Islamist crackdown demanded by the army.
A key Welfare MP has also criticised the prime minister for not giving in to the powerful military, in a rare break in party solidarity.
The army, which sees itself as the guardian of Turkey's strict secularist system, is expected to pressure the government to carry out its demands at a National Security Council meeting on Saturday.
The generals' discontent has raised fears of military intervention. The army has staged three coups since 1960.
Tekdal challenged critics to oust the government democratically.
"There are certain legal and constitutional rules on forcing the government out. Everyone should stake their claim. Governments aren't formed or toppled just for this or that reason," he said.

The main opposition Motherland Party on Thursday requested a parliamentary probe into interior minister Meral Aksener for allegedly abusing her position in the removal of national police chief Alaadin Yuksel last month.

The motion could lead to a ballot in parliament within a month that would effectively be a vote of confidence in the government. Erbakan 's coalition with conservatives has already weathered a series of similar parliamentary challenges.
